per_shot.note: Shows the hall, not a wing: no Gallery or Vivarium visible, no threshold into them. Same flat beige box with a black ceiling band, and the only light pool is the suit's own.

Plinths and placards are there and the stones are distinct colours, but the stones are flat unlit cones with no glow or facets, and nothing is lit like a museum piece. No spot pools, no glass, and the wall and floor are untouched by any of it.

The glass tanks read as cylinders, but they hold tiny confetti specks rather than creatures, and their light doesn't spill onto the floor, wall or glass. The room stays dim beige and the tanks look murky rather than alive.

top_issues.issue: Exhibits emit no light that lands
top_issues.why: The brief's core ask for the wings is pools of light and living light landing on the room. Right now the stones and creatures sit on the surface like stickers, and the wall, floor, plinth tops and tank bases stay at the same flat value as the hall.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each stone a narrow warm downlight from a ceiling fixture plus its own soft hue-matched point light, so there's a coloured wash on the plinth top, the placard and the wall behind it. Give each tank an emissive interior glow in its creature's hue that spills a coloured pool onto the floor in front and rims the glass edges. Darken the room between exhibits so the pools carry it.

top_issues.issue: Creatures in the tanks are unreadable specks
top_issues.why: At play scale the contents read as scattered particles. None of them reads as a creature (serpent, rimewing, polyp), so the 'remembered as light' idea comes across as noise instead of a showpiece.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Show one larger glowing low-poly silhouette per tank, a recognisable ribbon or wing or bloom shape built from emissive facets, drifting slowly. Add a soft bloom halo and a faint tinted fill (fog or water volume) in the tank so the glass reads as lit from inside.

top_issues.issue: Gallery stones look flat and unfaceted
top_issues.why: The stones are uniformly shaded cones with no faceting, specular glints or inner glow. They read as placeholder icons rather than cut, prized gems, and they lose the low-poly faceted house style.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Use cut-gem geometry (a few large facets) with flat-shaded light and dark faces, an emissive core and a bloom halo, and a slow rotation so the facets catch the downlight. Optionally add a glass vitrine box over each plinth with a bright edge highlight.

top_issues.issue: The wings share the hall's flat box and black ceiling
top_issues.why: The wings don't feel like distinct, more special rooms. The same single-value beige wall, red stripe and black ceiling slab carry through, which is exactly the 'basic box' complaint, and nothing marks the wings as showpieces.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Give each wing its own treatment: the Gallery gets darker walls (deep slate or plum) with a picture rail and track lights in a real ceiling, the Vivarium gets dark teal-black walls lit mainly by the tanks. Add panel seams, ribs and a visible ceiling with fixtures in place of the black band.

top_issues.issue: Plinths and tank bases are pure black masses
top_issues.why: Black is reserved for true void. Pure-black plinths and bases absorb the exhibit light and read as holes, and the floor in front of them has no reflection or pool to ground them.
top_issues.suggested_direction: Lift the plinths to dark stone or bronze with lit top edges and a rim from the exhibit light. Make the tank bases dark metal with an emissive trim ring, and let a subtle floor sheen show the coloured pools.

protect: One exhibit per fixed slot with a readable placard (name and depth band) at play scale
Distinct per-stone colours that map to the ores
Tank silhouettes reading as glass cylinders with rims
Dusk portholes as warm accents in the wall
The suit as the most legible thing in the frame, with its own floor pool
Side-view camera and low-poly procedural style
